title: Slice the food with a chef knife (Franka, operational-space control)
text: A carrot lies on a chopping board on a kitchen island; a chef knife lies on a knife rest beside the board. The carrot is scored at 7 transverse planes. Goal: pick up the knife and press its edge down through each scored plane (blade aligned with the plane) to cut the carrot into slices. The carrot is cut once every plane has been pressed through and the pieces separate, all of them staying on the board.
success: Success, exactly: at the end of the run the carrot is in 8 separate pieces. All 7 of its scored transverse joints have been released [`pieces_count() >= 8`]. The centre (vertex-mean centroid) of every piece lies over the chopping board: within 0.30 m of the board's centre along its long side, within 0.13 m along its short side, and above the board's top surface (0.882 m above the floor). A plane releases, permanently, at the first instant all of these hold, measured in the carrot's live frame (anchored on its fifth piece): the knife edge, at its point nearest that plane's flesh centre, is within 6 mm of the plane and within 25 mm of the flesh centre across the carrot; the blade face is within 15° of parallel to the plane; the edge is lower than the higher of the flesh centre's height and 1.5 mm above the board top; every piece moves under 0.10 m/s; and the knife rises no faster than 0.02 m/s. Not true at the start.
